paragraphs: An internship is a period of work experience offered by an organization for a limited period of time. Once confined to medical graduates, internship is used to practice for a wide range of placements in businesses, non-profit organizations, government agencies and political parties. They are typically undertaken by students and graduates looking to gain relevant skills and experience in a particular field. Employers benefit from these placements because they often recruit employees from their best interns, who have known capabilities, thus saving time and money in the long run. Internships are usually arranged by third-party organizations that recruit interns on behalf of industry groups. Rules vary from country to country about when interns should be regarded as employees. The system can be open to exploitation by unscrupulous employers.

Internships for professional careers are similar in some ways. Similar to internships, apprenticeships transition students from vocational school into the workforce. The lack of standardization and oversight leaves the term "internship" open to broad interpretation. Interns may be high school students, college and university students, or post-graduate adults. These positions may be paid or unpaid and are temporary. Many large corporations, particularly investment banks, have "insights" programs that serve as a pre-internship event numbering a day to a week, either in person or virtually.

Typically, an internship consists of an exchange of services for experience between the intern and the organization. Internships are used to determine whether the intern still has an interest in that field after real-life experience. In addition, an internship can be used to build a professional network that can assist with letters of recommendation or lead to future employment opportunities. The benefit of bringing an intern into full-time employment is that they are already familiar with the company, therefore requiring little to no training. Internships provide current college students with the ability to participate in a field of their choice, allowing them to receive hands-on learning about a particular future career and preparing them for full-time work following graduation.

questions.prompt: 根据文章，雇主将表现优秀的实习生转为正式员工有什么优势？
options: 已了解其能力，且其熟悉公司，因此能节省招聘或培训成本
优秀实习生更适合在与原实习无关的岗位立即任职
第三方机构会承担实习生转正后的全部培训工作
正式录用后，雇主可以延长实习安排而无需重新评估能力
questions.explanation: 第一段说优秀实习生的能力已知，招聘他们可节省时间和金钱；第三段补充，他们熟悉公司，所需培训很少甚至不需要培训。文中没有保证其适应所有岗位。
hints: 区分原因与结果，不要把相关现象直接当作因果。
回到第 1、3 段，逐项核对主体、范围及表示条件或程度的词。

questions.prompt: 除获得实际工作经验外，文章还指出实习能帮助实习生做什么？
options: 通过实习年限自动获得未来正式岗位的优先录用权
用一次实习替代职业学校所要求的全部培训
检验自己对该领域的兴趣，并建立职业人脉
获得与正式员工相同的身份，而不受所在地规则影响
questions.explanation: 第三段指出，真实工作经历可以帮助实习生判断是否仍对该领域感兴趣；实习也能建立 professional network，为推荐信或未来就业机会提供帮助。

sentence.text: Employers benefit from these placements because they often recruit employees from their best interns, who have known capabilities, thus saving time and money in the long run.
sentence.translation: 雇主从这些实习安排中受益，因为他们常从最优秀的实习生中招聘员工，而这些实习生的能力已为雇主所了解，从而在长远上节省时间和金钱。
sentence.analysis: 主干是 Employers benefit from these placements，because 引导原因状语从句。who have known capabilities 是非限制性定语从句，补充说明 their best interns；known 作形容词，表示能力已被了解。thus saving time and money 是现在分词短语，表示上述招聘做法带来的结果；in the long run 意为“从长远来看”。
